extra.message: User-controlled 'title' from the request body is concatenated directly into a shell command string executed via ProcessBuilder("/bin/sh", "-c", cmd). An attacker with API key or session access can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '; rm -rf /; #') to achieve arbitrary OS command execution.

The content of an uploaded 'rule' file is read as a raw string and evaluated directly with SpelExpressionParser().parseExpression(ruleExpr).getValue(row). Spring Expression Language is Turing-complete and can invoke arbitrary Java (e.g. T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec(...)), giving remote code execution to anyone who can supply the optional pricing-rule file on a unit import.

The HV_DASHBOARD_LAYOUT cookie value is base64-decoded and passed straight to java.io.ObjectInputStream.readObject(), deserializing fully attacker-controlled bytes. A crafted cookie containing a known gadget chain (e.g. via commons-collections, if present on the classpath) can achieve remote code execution; at minimum it is an insecure deserialization sink reachable pre-authentication via any cookie value.

JWT.decode(assertion) (auth0 java-jwt) only decodes the token's claims without verifying its signature. The 'email' claim is then trusted to look up and sign in as that user (lines 37-44) with no signature check and no issuer/audience validation. An attacker can forge an HV_OWNER_PORTAL_ASSERTION cookie with an arbitrary email claim and authenticate as any enabled user, including PROPERTY_ADMIN.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: The HV_WORKSPACE_VIEW cookie is only base64-encoded (not signed or encrypted) and carries the access level ('VIEWER' vs 'STAFF') used at line 263 to decide whether to return the ticket's internal resolutionSummary. Any caller can set this cookie directly to 'anything|STAFF' to read internal-only ticket data for any ticket key without authentication (the /tickets/share/** path is permitAll in SecurityConfig).

'/payments/receipt-access' is permitAll in SecurityConfig. requestReceipt() looks up a payment purely by its 'reference' string (PaymentService.findByReference, no ownership/identity check) and issues a receipt pass cookie, which paymentService.getForReceipt() then accepts in lieu of any authentication. Anyone who knows or guesses a payment reference can view another tenant's full receipt (name, lease, amount) with zero authentication.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The 'city' value from the request body is concatenated directly into an XPath expression string ('//listing[city=\'' + city + '\']') passed to dom4j's selectNodes. An attacker-controlled city value can break out of the string literal to alter the query logic (XPath injection), and the feed XML itself is parsed with org.dom4j.DocumentHelper.parseText without disabling external entity resolution, additionally exposing the endpoint to XXE.

org.dom4j.DocumentHelper.parseText(feed) parses fully attacker-supplied XML ('feedXml' from the request body) with dom4j's default SAXReader configuration, which does not disable DOCTYPE/external entity processing. This allows XXE attacks (local file disclosure, SSRF via external DTD) through the partner listings search endpoint.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: javax.xml.stream.XMLInputFactory.newInstance() is used with default settings (no IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false) to parse the attacker-supplied 'vendorMetadataXml' field, then fully consumed with reader.next(). Depending on the StAX implementation this can resolve external entities or DTDs embedded in the partner-supplied XML, enabling XXE-based file disclosure or SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The 'noteTemplate' field from the request body is compiled and executed directly as a Handlebars template via Handlebars().compileInline(template).apply(...). A caller holding any 'tickets:update'-scoped API key can supply arbitrary Handlebars syntax/helpers, which is evaluated server-side (server-side template injection) and the output is archived as a ticket comment.

The 'folder' value from the request body is resolved against the storage root with root.resolve(sub) and never normalized or checked for '..' traversal before being listed with java.nio.file.Files.list(p). A caller can supply a path such as '../../../../etc' to enumerate the contents of arbitrary directories on the filesystem outside the intended upload root.

attachRawReportFile() resolves the target path with reportsDir.resolve(file.originalFilename ?: "report") using the client-supplied multipart filename verbatim, with no sanitization and bypassing FileStorageService.validateUpload's extension allow-list (noted explicitly in the surrounding comment). A filename containing '..' path segments can write the uploaded file outside the intended inspection-reports/{category} directory.

The 'sourceUrl' field supplied on document upload is fetched directly with RestTemplate.getForEntity(url, ...) with no allow-list and no rejection of private/loopback/link-local addresses, letting a manager/admin make the server issue arbitrary HTTP requests to internal services (e.g. cloud metadata endpoints, internal admin panels) and store the response as a document.

uploadEvidenceFromUrl() opens an HttpURLConnection directly against the caller-supplied 'sourceUrl' with no host allow-list or private/loopback rejection (explicitly called out in the method's own doc comment), allowing SSRF against internal network services reachable from the application server.

The Referer request header is written directly into the HTML response body ('$back') without any HTML-encoding. Since the Referer header is attacker-controllable by crafting the referring page's URL, this allows reflected cross-site scripting against any user who follows a link to /resume from an attacker-controlled page.
response.sendRedirect(target) redirects to the raw Referer header value with no same-origin or allow-list validation, enabling an open redirect through the trusted application domain for phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: @CrossOrigin(originPatterns = ["*"], allowCredentials = "true") permits any origin to make credentialed (cookie-authenticated) cross-origin requests to the dashboard overview endpoint, letting any malicious website read a signed-in user's role-specific dashboard data (property counts, revenue, occupancy) via the victim's browser session.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: After accepting an invite, the method manually installs the new SecurityContext into whatever session already exists (request.getSession(true) returns the pre-existing session rather than a freshly-rotated one) instead of going through Spring Security's authentication flow, which the app otherwise configures with changeSessionId() (SecurityConfig.kt). A session ID fixed/known to an attacker before the victim authenticates remains valid afterward.

The same manual SecurityContext installation pattern as AuthController is used here for the owner-portal handoff: request.getSession(true) reuses any pre-existing session instead of rotating the session identifier, bypassing the application's configured sessionFixation().changeSessionId() protection and allowing a fixated session to become authenticated.

enableKioskPass() replaces the account's bcrypt password hash with an unsalted MD5 digest of the kiosk cookie value ({md5}+DigestUtils.md5Hex(...)), which PortalCredentialEncoder.matches() then accepts for the main login credential. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsalted, making the stored verifier trivial to crack via rainbow tables if the database is ever disclosed, and it downgrades the account's authentication strength below bcrypt.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: postToLedgerBridge() reads the live JSESSIONID cookie off the current request and forwards it as a URL query parameter ('?session=$sessionRef') to an internal HTTP (not HTTPS) endpoint. Placing a live session identifier in a URL and sending it in cleartext exposes it to logging/caching along the path and effectively hands the recipient service the ability to impersonate the current user's session.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: submitToRecordsDesk() takes the current request's JSESSIONID cookie value and sends it as an 'Authorization: Bearer' header to an internal HTTP endpoint. The live portal session token is reused as a bearer credential for a separate system over plaintext HTTP, exposing it to interception and letting that system impersonate the user.

The HV_PORTAL_SESSION cookie value is read from the request and written to the application log via log.info. If this cookie carries session or tracking identifiers, persisting it in logs (which typically have broader access than the application itself) is an information disclosure risk.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: On a failed API key lookup, the raw presented key value is written to the application log ('presented key {}', rawKey). Logging full secret values on failed authentication exposes near-miss or leaked keys to anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The receipt view explicitly clears the X-Frame-Options header ('') so the page can be iframed by any site. Combined with the weak reference/pass-based access to this endpoint, this removes clickjacking protection on a page displaying tenant PII and payment data.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: '/documents/*/pickup' is permitAll in SecurityConfig and is protected only by a 6-digit numeric code (DocumentService.pickupCodeMatches) compared with no rate limiting or lockout. An unauthenticated attacker can brute-force the ~900,000 possible codes to download tenant-visible documents for an arbitrary document id.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: A single hardcoded password ("Harborview123!") is assigned to every seeded account across all roles including PROPERTY_ADMIN, and a hardcoded demo API key value ('hv_demo_reader_key_2026', line 270) and webhook signing secret ('demo-webhook-secret', line 282) are embedded in source. Low severity since this path only runs when the database is empty (demo/seed data), but if accidentally enabled against a real deployment these are guessable, well-known credentials.

The 'X-Staff-Ref' header value is concatenated directly into an LDAP search filter string ('(&(objectClass=person)(uid=' + staffRef + '))') with no escaping of LDAP special characters, allowing filter injection to broaden or alter the directory search performed against the internal staff directory.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query
